column1: # How each failing case of the computed-value gate (tools/conformance/css_computed_suite.py) is listed. tools/conformance/classify-computed.py reads this table and the
# failures the gate reports, and writes CSS_COMPUTED_EXCEPTIONS and CSS_COMPUTED_DEFECTS; a failure no row matches is an error, and so is a row no failure matches.
#   <property regex> TAB <answer regex> TAB <kind> TAB <class or owner> TAB <reason or what the library lacks>
# The property regex is matched in full against the property (the page's, dashed); the answer regex is searched in what the library answered (".*" for any). kind is
# `exception` (the class is one of tools/conformance/css_computed_suite.py's) or `defect` (the owner is the piece of work that closes it). The first row that matches wins.
# Served text quoted for resolved-value (CSSOM, "Resolved Values", drafts.csswg.org/cssom, served 2026-10-27): "The resolved value is the computed value." for any other
# property, and for the properties that have a special case: "then the resolved value is the used value." (the size, margin, padding and inset properties, the colors
# that are `currentcolor`, line-height, the grid track lists, transform-origin and perspective-origin's percentages: a value that depends on layout).

column5: the served text does not say how path data is written once computed; the page for clip-path keeps the commands, the page for shape-outside writes them absolute, Chromium writes absolute commands and Firefox keeps the written ones: kept as written [record: *]
the page is tentative: its expectations are those of a draft that the standard does not yet hold

the computed value of the longhand keeps the origin keyword: Backgrounds 4, 2.6: "A list, each item consisting of: an offset given as a computed <length-percentage> value, plus an origin keyword"; the page and both pinned browsers drop it (`right 25%` is `75%`) [record: *]
the computed value has three values: Text 4 (property table): "three values, each either the auto keyword or an integer"; the page and both pinned browsers write the shortest form [record: *]

the computed value is a pair: Text Decoration 4 (property table): "the keyword none, a pair of keywords representing the shape and fill, or a string"; the page and both pinned browsers drop the default `filled` [record: *]

the computed value keeps what was specified: Text Decoration 4 (property table): "Computed value: specified keyword(s)"; the page and both pinned browsers drop the default side of the writing mode [record: *]

the computed value keeps what was specified: Overflow 5 (property table): "Computed value: specified keyword(s)"; the page writes `before links` (Chromium does; Firefox has no such property) [record: *]
`auto` is a computed value: Animations 2 (property table): "list, each item either a time or the keyword auto"; the page and both pinned browsers write `0s` [record: *]
the computed value is two lengths: Tables 3 (property table): "Computed value: two absolute lengths"; the page and both pinned browsers write one when they are equal [record: *]

the computed value is as specified: Masking 1 (property table for clip): "Computed value: as specified"; the page and both pinned browsers write the lengths absolute and a calculation evaluated [record: *]
a zero term of a sum is kept: Values 4, 10.10: "Zero-valued terms cannot be simply removed from a Sum"; the page and both pinned browsers write `calc(10% + 0px)` as `10%` [record: *]
the computed value is as specified: Fonts 4 (property table): "Computed value: as specified"; the page and both pinned browsers sort the features by tag [record: *]

`oblique-only` is not a keyword of the shorthand: Fonts 4: "none | [ weight || style || small-caps || position ]"; it is a keyword of font-synthesis-style; the page and Firefox accept it, Chromium refuses it [record: *]

a number is written with no more than six decimals: CSSOM 6.7.2: "rounding the value if necessary to not produce more than 6 decimals"; the page and both pinned browsers write six significant digits (`11.4592deg`) [record: *]

a radius is one or two extents or one or two lengths, not both: Images 4: "<radial-size> = <radial-extent>{1,2} | <length-percentage [0,∞]>{1,2}"; the page and both pinned browsers accept `ellipse(1px closest-side)` [record: *]
the track list of a grid container resolves to the used track sizes, and to `none` where the element is not a grid container: "then the resolved value is the used value."
a percentage resolves against the box (the 200 by 300 pixel box of the page): "then the resolved value is the used value."
a percentage or a calculation with one resolves to the used length: "then the resolved value is the used value."
the size of a box resolves to its used size: "then the resolved value is the used value."
a number resolves to the used length: "then the resolved value is the used value."
a pair of equal lengths is written as one value (the shortest serialization the page expects, Text Decoration 4); the computed value is the pair
`currentcolor` resolves to the used color of the element: "then the resolved value is the used value."
the property is classified unimplemented (the 15 listed in the plan: -webkit-box-*, -webkit-user-select, corner-*-shape, position-area)
`corner-*` and the `corner-*-shape` longhands are unimplemented
unimplemented, or the initial value of a newer draft
a gradient is not written in its computed form (default position and shape omitted, positions and sizes made absolute, a color stop in sRGB): the image functions are specified values
the arguments of a filter function are not computed (blur() is blur(0px), a percentage amount is a number, calc() is simplified)
a basic shape is not written in its computed form (rect() and xywh() as inset(), `center` as 50%, a ray's angle in degrees)

the computed value of this property is written differently from the page's expectation: a newer draft than the pin, a shortest form, a default that is written, or a computation that is not done (the page's expectation is in the list of the case)
